title: Completing a polynomial presentation preserves its conormal differential
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], $I\subseteq A$ an ideal, $S=A[x_1,\ldots,x_r]$ for an integer $r\geq0$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], and $\alpha:S\twoheadrightarrow B$ a surjective homomorphism of commutative $A$-algebras with finitely generated kernel $K$. Write $P=\varprojlim_n S/I^nS$ and $\widehat B=\varprojlim_n B/I^nB$ for the adic completions [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], and let $\widehat\alpha:P\to\widehat B$ be the map induced by $\alpha$ on compatible sequences. Then $\widehat\alpha$ is surjective, its kernel is $J=KP$ (the ideal generated by the image of $K$), and the canonical map $(K/K^2)\otimes_B\widehat B\to J/J^2$, $\bar k\otimes b\mapsto b\bar k$, is an isomorphism [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Polynomial differentiation [def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative] induces continuous partial derivatives on $P$ by differentiating each coordinate modulo $I^nS$. The maps $d_0:K/K^2\to B^{\oplus r}$, $\bar f\mapsto(\alpha(\partial f/\partial x_i))_i$, and $\widehat d:J/J^2\to\widehat B^{\oplus r}$, $\bar f\mapsto(\widehat\alpha(\partial f/\partial x_i))_i$, are well-defined linear maps over $B$ and $\widehat B$, respectively. Under the displayed conormal isomorphism and the canonical identification $B^{\oplus r}\otimes_B\widehat B\cong\widehat B^{\oplus r}$, one has $\widehat d=d_0\otimes_B\widehat B$.

source.place: Tag 0GAF (lemma-NL-is-completion), statement and proof: completion is exact on finite modules, the completed presentation has kernel K^wedge=KP, and (K/K^2) tensor_B B^wedge = K^wedge/(K^wedge)^2; equation-NL specifies the continuous partial-derivative differential.

proof.text: Put $L=IS\subseteq S$ and $M=K/K^2$. The finite polynomial algebra $S$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], applied to the presentation $S=A[x_1,\ldots,x_r]/(0)$ of [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. Choose ideal generators $k_1,\ldots,k_t$ of $K$. As $S$-modules, $S$ is generated by $1$, $B$ by $1$, $K$ by the $k_a$, $K^2$ by the finitely many $k_ak_b$, and $M$ by the classes of the $k_a$. Thus all modules used below are finite over the Noetherian ring $S$. For any $S$-module $N$, expansion of products of elements of $IS$ gives $L^nN=I^nN$. In particular completion of $B$ as an $S$-module at $L$ is exactly the displayed $\widehat B$, and completion of $S$ is $P$. The map $S/K\to B$, $s+K\mapsto\alpha(s)$, is bijective because $\alpha$ is surjective with kernel $K$; use this identification for scalar actions.

source.place: Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence); setup for Tag 00MA (lemma-completion-tensor), as used by restricted.tex Tag 0GAF (lemma-NL-is-completion).

proof.text: Complete the short exact sequence $0\to K\to S\xrightarrow{\alpha}B\to0$ at $L$. By [lem-weil-pbc-completion-exact-finite-modules] its completion is $0\to K^\wedge\to P\xrightarrow{\widehat\alpha}\widehat B\to0$, with the displayed coordinatewise map $\widehat\alpha$. By [lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-module-tensor], $P\otimes_SK\to K^\wedge$, $p\otimes k\mapsto p\,\iota_K(k)$, is an isomorphism, natural for $K\hookrightarrow S$. Therefore its composite into $P$ sends $p\otimes k$ to $p\,\iota_S(k)$. Its image is precisely the set of finite sums of such products, namely $KP$. Consequently $\widehat\alpha$ is surjective, $\ker\widehat\alpha=J=KP$, and the inclusion identifies $K^\wedge$ with $J$. The induced ring map $P/J\to\widehat B$ is bijective: surjectivity is that of $\widehat\alpha$ and equality of two images means their difference belongs to $J$.

source.place: Tag 0GAF (lemma-NL-is-completion), proof: completed presentation; algebra.tex Tags 00MA (lemma-completion-tensor) and 00MB (lemma-completion-flat).

proof.text: Complete $0\to K^2\to K\to M\to0$. The exactness statement [lem-weil-pbc-completion-exact-finite-modules] identifies $M^\wedge$ with $K^\wedge/\operatorname{im}((K^2)^\wedge)$. The natural tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-module-tensor] for $K^2\hookrightarrow S$ shows that the image of $(K^2)^\wedge$ in $P$ is $K^2P$. Since $K^\wedge\to P$ is injective by Step 2, the submodule being divided out corresponds inside $J$ exactly to $K^2P$. Products of finite sums $p\,\iota_S(k)$ show $(KP)^2\subseteq K^2P$, while each generator $p\,\iota_S(kk')=(p\,\iota_S(k))\iota_S(k')$ proves the reverse inclusion. Thus $K^2P=J^2$ and we obtain the $P$-linear isomorphism $M^\wedge\xrightarrow{\sim}J/J^2$ taking the completion image of $k+K^2$ to $\iota_S(k)+J^2$.

source.place: Tag 0GAF (lemma-NL-is-completion), proof, displayed conormal equality; algebra.tex Tag 00MA (lemma-completion-tensor), parts (2) and (3).

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-module-tensor], $M^\wedge\cong P\otimes_SM$. The elementary change of scalar-ring identification here is $P\otimes_SM\xrightarrow{\sim}M\otimes_B\widehat B$, $p\otimes m\mapsto m\otimes\widehat\alpha(p)$. To construct its inverse, choose $p$ lifting $b\in\widehat B$ and send $m\otimes b$ to $p\otimes m$. If the lift changes by $\sum_a p_a\iota_S(k_a)$, its tensor with $m$ changes by $\sum_a p_a\otimes k_am=0$, since $KM=0$. For $s\in S$, the balancing relation is $p\iota_S(s)\otimes m=p\otimes sm$; it proves $B$-balancing because $S\twoheadrightarrow B$. Additivity follows by choosing sums of lifts. These formulas define inverse linear maps by the tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Combining them with Step 3 gives the asserted isomorphism $M\otimes_B\widehat B\to J/J^2$, $\bar k\otimes b\mapsto b\,\overline{\iota_S(k)}$.

source.place: Tag 0GAF (lemma-NL-is-completion), proof, displayed conormal equality; algebra.tex Tag 00MA (lemma-completion-tensor), part (3), with the tensor balancing spelled out.

proof.text: For each $i$, let $D_i=\partial/\partial x_i$ from [def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative]. It is $A$-linear, so $D_i(\sum_a a_as_a)=\sum_a a_aD_i(s_a)$ for $a_a\in I^n$, whence $D_i(I^nS)\subseteq I^nS$. It therefore induces an $A$-linear operator $D_{i,n}$ on $S/I^nS$. These operators commute with quotient transition maps, since all are induced by the same $D_i$. On the compatible-sequence completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], define $\widehat D_i((f_n)_n)=(D_{i,n}(f_n))_n$. The Leibniz rule holds coordinatewise, as does $\widehat D_i(\iota_S(f))=\iota_S(D_i(f))$. For the inverse-limit topology (each quotient discrete), every kernel of a coordinate projection is preserved, which proves continuity. This constructs precisely the partial derivatives asserted in the statement.

source.place: Equation (equation-NL), continuous partial derivatives, and Tag 0GAF (lemma-NL-is-completion), identification of the differentials; polynomial derivations as in algebra.tex Tag 00RX (lemma-differentials-polynomial-ring).

proof.text: The product rule from [def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative] gives $D_i(uv)=uD_i(v)+vD_i(u)\in K$ for $u,v\in K$. Hence $f\mapsto(\alpha(D_i(f)))_i$ kills $K^2$. For $s\in S$ and $f\in K$, $\alpha(D_i(sf))=\alpha(s)\alpha(D_i(f))$, since the remaining term contains $\alpha(f)=0$. This proves that $d_0$ is well defined and $B$-linear, since every $B$-scalar lifts to $S$. By the coordinatewise product rule of Step 5, $\widehat D_i(uv)\in J$ for $u,v\in J$, and for $p\in P$, $f\in J$ we have $\widehat\alpha(\widehat D_i(pf))=\widehat\alpha(p)\widehat\alpha(\widehat D_i(f))$. These identities prove that the completed formula kills $J^2$ and is linear over $P/J=\widehat B$. Thus $\widehat d$ is also a well-defined linear map.

source.place: Equation (equation-NL) and Tag 0GAF (lemma-NL-is-completion), the conormal differentials; explicit product-rule verification.

proof.text:
Identify $B^{\oplus r}\otimes_B\widehat B$ with $\widehat B^{\oplus r}$ by $v\otimes b\mapsto(bv_i)_i$; the inverse sends $(b_i)_i$ to $\sum_{i=1}^r e_i\otimes b_i$. The tensor relations [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product] show directly these maps are inverse, also for $r=0$ where the sum is empty. For $k\in K$ and $b\in\widehat B$, choose $p\in P$ with $\widehat\alpha(p)=b$. Step 4 sends $\bar k\otimes b$ to $\overline{p\iota_S(k)}$. By the product rule [def-weil-pbc-polynomial-partial-derivative] extended in Step 5, its $i$-th differential coordinate is
$$\widehat\alpha(\widehat D_i(p)\iota_S(k)+p\iota_S(D_i(k)))=b\,\iota_B(\alpha(D_i(k))),$$
because $\widehat\alpha(\iota_S(k))=0$; here $\iota_B:B\to\widehat B$ is the coordinatewise completion map. This is the $i$-th coordinate of $(d_0\otimes_B\widehat B)(\bar k\otimes b)$. Pure tensors generate, and both maps are $\widehat B$-linear by Step 6, so equality on these elements proves the asserted equality of differentials.
